answers.explanation: Ordering and retransmission come from TCP underneath.
Each side sends half, and both derive the same keys.
The server also signs the handshake with the certificate's private key to prove it holds it.
Ephemeral keys are thrown away after the handshake. TLS 1.3 requires it.
Session resumption lets returning clients skip most of it.
A replayed GET is harmless; a replayed payment isn't.
